summary: PASS. Log stores rewritten to _qlog[0..2]; (s32)arg cast matches the s32 record type. Object model verified: e8d8684b8 records SYS .data XDEFs _qlog +0x144 / _qin +0x154, so _qlog runs 0x8009BF68..77; asm has no access to word 3, so the '[3] is never read' claim is true. Volatile: the _qlog row in volatile_extern_allowlist.txt grants the symbol (grants are per symbol per legitimate-volatile-interrupt-touched.md), and under the one-object model the symbol is the whole 16-byte record; C cannot make one element volatile. _qlog really is written from _exeque, which is the DMA-2 IRQ callback (DMACallback(2,_exeque)). The volatile also carries load: I compiled a reviewer probe with only the volatile removed. It routes words 1-2 through word 0's base register (sw 4/8(s0)) and sinks a store into a delay slot (_exeque 44, _addque2 25, get_alarm 11 differing objdump lines). The target's separate lui/%lo accesses for words 1-2 match the all-volatile reading. So this is the granted volatile on its true extent, not a new barrier, and it retires a FAKE do-while(0) (item 5: fewer FAKEs). The asm/funcs listing edits keep addresses (_qlog=0x8009BF68, +4=BF6C, +8=BF70, encoded bytes unchanged). No D_8009BF6C/70/74 references remain in src/asm/include. sandbox --disable all = 0 after a fresh make (bb2.exe OK). Hygiene debt: the allowlist _qlog row's codegen-prong text still cites 'non-volatile adjacent siblings D_8009BF6C and D_8009BF70', which is now stale and should be reworded for the whole record; the symbol_addrs.txt D_8009BF6C/D_8009BF70 rows are kept.
